correctness.rationale: The graph neighborhood predicate is derived directly from the undirected shift graph. Unique nonzero mask intersections are logically equivalent to closed-neighborhood identifying codes. Exhaustion of all 2,220,075 eight-subsets and 4,686,825 nine-subsets proves minimum nine and exactly 4,366 nine-code equality cases. Nine fixed and nine paired reversal orbits yield an exhaustive 2^18-set invariant search, showing minimum eleven and 117 equality cases. Two independent implementations, explicit witnesses, and regenerated natural-group representative files were checked. The result is finite only.

value.rationale: Orientation reversal is a graph automorphism and a natural physical design constraint for network sensing. The demonstrated two-sensor cost, from nine to eleven, is a 22.2% increase and establishes an exact finite symmetry-breaking boundary. The complete equality populations and symmetry-orbit classifications quantify alternative placements and are not implied by the known minimum size. The object and symmetry condition are natural, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
